hook: Weak shower pressure? $29.94 fixes scale buildup, not plumbing.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of a trickling showerhead, water barely dripping, slightly annoyed reaction shot
Macro-style shot of white mineral scale crusted inside a nozzle hole
scenes.on_screen_text: Hard water scale clogs the nozzle holes
scenes.voiceover: After three to five years, mineral scale quietly chokes the nozzle holes until you compare it to something better.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text graphic listing California, Colorado, and New York next to '1.8-2.0 GPM cap'
scenes.on_screen_text: Some states cap flow at 1.8 GPM
scenes.voiceover: California, Colorado, and New York now cap new fixtures at 1.8 to 2.0 gallons a minute — even lower than the federal rule.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of the AquaCare showerhead nozzle face, rubberized coating texture visible, price tag $29.94 overlay

scenes.visual_prompt: Split screen: weak dribble on left labeled 'before', strong spray on right labeled 'after'

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand toggling the wand between rinse mode and power-wash mode, water pattern changing
scenes.voiceover: Rinse mode for the kids, power wash for you.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final shot of the showerhead mounted on a shower arm, price sticker, link graphic
scenes.voiceover: It's the cheapest fix for scale that a plumber can't undo anyway.

caption: Your shower isn't broken, it's just full of scale and legally capped at 2.5 GPM. The $29.94 fix for that — full details in bio.
